intro: Trying to find Connecticut scholarships tied to financial need without wading into higher-award listings? This filtered slice narrows the search to USA programs with smaller award ranges, which can be useful if you want to apply broadly, compare several options, or add stackable aid to a larger funding plan. Requirements are not identical across the set: some may ask for essays, some appear lighter-touch, and eligibility details can differ by residency, school status, or field. Award amounts vary by listing, and deadlines differ by program, so it is worth checking each row promptly.

faq.question: Can I apply to more than one scholarship listed here?
faq.answer: Usually, you can explore and apply to multiple programs if you meet each listing’s requirements. Check every row individually, because rules, residency or citizenship details, and submission steps are set by the relevant provider.

faq.question: What should I compare before I apply?
faq.answer: Focus on award amount, deadline, study level, category, and any requirement notes shown in the catalog. ScholarshipTop highlights available deadline and award details in a structured format so you can prioritize opportunities and plan your next step.

faq.question: Are these only for college students in the USA?
faq.answer: Not necessarily—these rows can include different study levels such as high school seniors, sophomores, and graduate students. Some listings also show USA-specific eligibility like U.S. citizen or permanent resident, so read each scholarship carefully before you apply.
